newsitem.title: USA: Ford July U.S. vehicle sales seen best of Big 3.
newsitem.headline: Ford July U.S. vehicle sales seen best of Big 3.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. is expected to post the best July U.S. vehicle sales among the Big Three automakers, thanks to robust truck sales that include some high-profile customers for its imposing new Lincoln Navigator.

Buyers of the Navigator, a large, luxury sport utility vehicle, include actors Arnold Schwarzenegger and Warren Beatty, as well as professional basketball stars Michael Jordan and Shaquille O'Neal, according to James O'Connor, general manager of the Lincoln-Mercury division.
The Navigator, which starts at $39,950 for two-wheel drive and $43,300 for four-wheel-drive versions, went on sale on July 1. So far, Ford has received 19,000 orders, O'Connor said.
Ford is scheduled to report July sales on Aug. 5. General Motors Corp. and Chrysler Corp. are expected to release results on Aug. 1.

Ford's truck sales are some of the strongest in the industry, and Credit Suisse First Boston analyst Nicholas Colas predicted they rose 7.5 percent in July, offsetting an equal decline in passenger cars for a flat total.
Ford Automotive Operations President Jacques Nasser said earlier this week the company's U.S. July sales will improve over its June results, when it posted a light vehicle sales gain of 4.7 percent.

Total U.S. July light vehicle sales are expected to be down about 2 percent from a year ago as the industry maintains the second-quarter trend of softer sales. The July seasonally adjusted annual sales rate is forecast at 14.4 million or 14.5 million, down from last year's 14.7 million but up from June's 14.3 million.
Sales from GM and Chrysler are expected to fall. Large Japanese automakers, which have enjoyed consistently strong sales all year, are seen gaining further in market share, analysts said.

Car and truck sales from the U.S. No. 1 automaker, which tumbled 13.5 percent in June, are seen falling about 4 percent from July 1996 as the company recovers from the effects of work stoppages, according to analysts.
GM's car sales will be down 4 percent to 8 percent, while analysts were divided on whether the company's truck sales will rise or fall slightly.
Colas noted that GM has changed the dealer incentives for selling outgoing model year vehicles to clear them out earlier than normal before the start of the 1998 model year, which starts in October.
"This will likely boost GM's share in the month, but potentially at the expense of future months in the year," he said in a sales report.
Burnham Securities Inc. analyst David Healy said GM's market share will be about 29 percent in July, an improvement over its record low 28.4 percent in June.
"GM's market share looks weak again in July, but probably not as bad as June," he said.

Chrysler's sales, up against strong year-ago comparisons, will fall between 7 percent and 9 percent, analysts said. Healy said both cars and trucks will fall at the U.S. No. 3 automaker, which has an ageing product line-up compared with other members of the Big Three.
